note: House schema (ads-doctrine tenants): routines -> phases -> steps. A phase has a `gate` stated in words - the condition that must be true to leave it. A step is MACHINE (a command, and it must name the field or file it reads), AGENT (judgement, and it must name its evidence) or PRINCIPLE (a standing rule). `killer: true` means skipping it has actually cost us a session.

routines.title: Make a film
routines.when: Any new video composition, or a substantial re-direction of an existing one.

phases.title: 1 · Measure the brief
phases.why: A brief that fixes a duration AND supplies the words is over-constrained until someone multiplies one out against the other. Nobody ever does, because the two halves read as equally authoritative and never sit side by side.
phases.gate: Speech/beat time has been computed against the stated runtime, and any conflict has been put to the operator as a priced choice - not silently resolved.

steps.text: Compute beats x seconds against the supplied copy before designing anything.
steps.field: cutsheet.json totalSeconds vs the sum of frame durations
steps.detail: 2026-08-10: a brief marked 90-105s NON-NEGOTIABLE shipped with a script measuring ~302s. Everything built before the conflict surfaced was built against the wrong film.

steps.text: Present the conflict as the operator's choice with both options priced: hold the duration and cut N% of the words, or hold the words and run to M seconds.
steps.evidence: the arithmetic from F1, stated in seconds

steps.text: Copy from a source is reproduced as found. Contradictions in the source are flagged, never reconciled by us.

phases.title: 2 · Declare the direction
phases.why: Without a stated restraint, every direction converges on the same shell, and the reflex fix for 'it feels flat' is to add effects - which is how a film becomes noisy rather than good.
phases.gate: One big idea and a restraint statement are written into the composition's own source, above the code, before any code exists.

steps.text: Write the ONE BIG IDEA in a sentence, and the RESTRAINT STATEMENT - what you will deliberately not do - as a docstring at the top of the composition.
steps.evidence: the docstring itself; a direction with no restraint is not ready to build

steps.text: Apply the grid-fallback test: if this were reduced to a plain centred layout, what idea would break? 'Not much' means the direction is not strong enough yet.
steps.evidence: a named idea that would be lost

steps.text: Type names what the picture has shown. If a beat only works because of its caption, the picture is not doing its job.

phases.title: 3 · Build
phases.why: The craft defects that make generated video read as generated are mechanical and greppable. There is no reason to find them by eye.
phases.gate: The doctrine linter is clean on the composition directory.

steps.text: Data (cutsheet, tokens) is shared across directions. Only the expression changes, or you are comparing different films.
Price the grade as you add it. feTurbulence at full resolution cost 1.68 s/frame - 21 minutes a render - until it was moved to 1/3 res and scaled up.

phases.title: 4 · Look at it
phases.why: Three of five defects in the last arm existed ONLY in the rendered artifact and zero were visible in source review. Stills at mid-segment frames are clean by construction.
phases.gate: Every camera move and every mount/unmount window has been RANGE-rendered and watched, not sampled as stills.

steps.text: npx remotion render ... --frames=A-B over each camera move, then actually watch it.
steps.field: the frame range of each move

steps.text: Same code, different output between a scoped and a full render means the ENVIRONMENT is the variable. Stop editing code; build the 2x2 over --gl, --concurrency and frame range.
steps.detail: rule 57. Five sessions of code refactoring, then a 15-minute matrix found it.

steps.text: For a reported visual artifact: render, zoom, and NAME the element before forming any theory.
steps.evidence: the named element and its source line

phases.title: 5 · Measure the artifact
phases.why: 'Better' is unfalsifiable without numbers, and numbers from an instrument nobody has watched fail are worse than none.
phases.gate: Both probes have run AND both negative-control batteries fired.

steps.text: Run both probes on every arm including the frozen baseline.
These are PROXIES. A metric that disagrees with the operator's eye is a wrong metric, not a wrong eye.

phases.title: 6 · Score
phases.why: A side-by-side glance is not reproducible and accumulates nothing. Position and label bias are large and free to remove.
phases.gate: Arms scored blind, in both orders, with the frozen baseline present in the set.

steps.text: Include a confound control - the baseline with ONLY the cheap change applied (e.g. music). Without it, a win cannot be attributed to craft.
Serve the pairs from a Range-capable server and verify the URL from Windows before handing it over.
Write the result to the ledger WITH numbers, so the next film can be compared to this one.
